title: Resource Allocation and Network Management with Edge AI
summary: Develop efficient AI for resource allocation and autonomous network management.
description: We study how learning algorithms can manage wireless and satellite resources and execute on edge hardware. Work connects algorithm design with experimental evaluation on AI accelerators.
approach: Reinforcement learning; Deep learning; Neuromorphic computing; Edge inference
applications: Satellite communications; Wireless resource allocation; Onboard signal processing
motivation: Network decisions must adapt quickly within limited power and computing budgets.

title: Semantic Communications for Earth Observation
summary: Transmit useful information from Earth observation data efficiently.
description: We explore AI methods that select, compress and reconstruct information for Earth observation tasks. Semantic processing links communication decisions to the information needed by downstream applications.
approach: Semantic representation learning; AI compression; Edge AI
applications: Earth observation; Inter-satellite communications; Environmental monitoring
motivation: Earth observation produces large datasets while satellite links and onboard power are constrained.

title: Data and AI Model Marketplace Ecosystems
summary: Support trustworthy sharing of data and AI models across digital ecosystems.
description: We investigate distributed learning and smart contracts for collaborative digital services. The aim is to support reliable collaboration among participants that hold different datasets and computing resources.
motivation: Collaborative AI requires dependable mechanisms for participation and exchange.

title: Open tools & datasets
description: This planned research direction aims to make experiments in AI-enabled wireless and satellite communications easier to reproduce, inspect, and extend. The focus is on connecting research code, data preparation, system assumptions, and evaluation protocols so that future studies can build on a clear experimental foundation.
approach: Develop documented simulation and evaluation tools, versioned experiment configurations, and data preparation workflows. Establish transparent baselines and reproducibility checklists; release code and datasets when ownership, licensing, and privacy requirements permit.
applications: Reusable benchmarks for wireless and satellite AI; reproducible edge-learning experiments; research software and educational materials.
imageAlt: Illustration of open research tools, datasets, and reproducible workflows
summary: A planned direction for reusable research software, documented datasets, and transparent evaluation of intelligent communication systems.
motivation: Comparisons between learning-based communication methods depend on data partitions, channel assumptions, implementation choices, and computing budgets. Making these choices explicit helps researchers understand when results transfer to another setting.
challenges: Documenting data provenance, licenses, and permitted uses
Keeping experimental configurations and software dependencies traceable
Comparing methods under consistent communication and computation budgets
Maintaining reusable resources as models and platforms evolve
